3.name: Unrelenting Force
entries: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you improve in your ability to manipulate your opponent in battle. You gain the ability to use the shove attack or the grapple attack as a bonus action by spending a point of Ki. Maintaining control of your opponent will give you the upper hand in battle, giving you and your allies a chance to inflict as much harm as possible.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) skill if you do not already have it.
You also gain proficiency in {@tool cook's utensils} if you don't already have it.

6.name: Improved Shove
entries: Starting at 6th level, you improve in your ability to push your opponent away or to the ground.
When performing a shove attack you can spend a Ki point to have advantage on the attack.
In addition, your distance to push an enemy increases to 10 ft.

11.name: Sumo Stomp
entries: At 11th level, as an action you can spend 2 Ki points to shake the earth. Those within 15 ft must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Ki save DC or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage and fall prone. On a success, they take half damage and remain standing.
You can spend additional Ki to increase the damage by 1d6 per point, up to a maximum of half your monk level.

17.name: Yokozuna
entries: At 17th level, as a bonus action you can use 3 Ki points to gain 2d6 temporary hit points that last for 1 minute. At the start of each turn, you may reroll the temporary hit points, replacing the current amount if it's higher.
You may dismiss this effect at any time.
